# MEASUREMENTS

Append-only run log for TurboFieldfare. Every real-model run gets one row.

## Rules

**Do not edit or delete an existing row.** Not to fix a typo, not to correct a number, not to tidy formatting. A row records what was observed at a moment on a specific commit; rewriting it destroys the only record of what was actually true then.

- To correct a row, append a new row and reference the superseded date + SHA in its notes.
- To retract a row, append a new row saying so. Leave the original.
- Rows are appended at the bottom, newest last.
- One row per run. Do not average several runs into a single row — append each, and note the relationship.
- Runs that failed, regressed, or disproved a prediction get rows too. A log that only contains wins is not a measurement record.
- Fill every column. Use `?` for genuinely unknown, never a guess or a carried-over value from an earlier row.

Accepted current values live in the Measured facts table in `CLAUDE.md`; when a row here supersedes one, update that table in the same change. What has been tried and why it was kept or abandoned goes in `docs/PRIOR_ART.md`.

## Column definitions

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Date | `YYYY-MM-DD` of the run. |
| SHA | Short git SHA of the checkout, plus `-dirty` if the tree was not clean. |
| Config | Host, then the controls that differ from production defaults (4K context, 16 slots, LFU, prefill on / 128-token chunks, RDADVISE off, temp `0.2` / Top-K `64` / Top-P `0.95`). Write `defaults` when nothing differs. |
| Bytes/token | Steady-state decode bytes read per token. Note prefill separately in notes; the two are not comparable. |
| Hit rate | Expert-cache hit rate over the measured window. |
| tok/s | Decode rate from the timing footer. |
| Thermal | `nominal` / `fair` / `serious` / `critical`, observed during the run. |
| Notes | Prediction vs. measured delta, prompt or benchmark used, anomalies, supersedes/retracts references. |

| 2026-08-10 | ce287b6 | M1 MacBook Air 8 GB, macOS 26.6.1 (25G76); host I/O probe suite, **no model run** — layer files opened `O_RDONLY`, never modified | n/a | n/a | n/a | nominal | **Diagnosis of the "41–50% of the device roof" fetch gap. Result: the gap does not exist — the 2026-08-10 roof was measured on compressible data.** Four standalone probes (sources in `Scripts/probes/`), model process not started, preflight clean, 44% memory free. **(1) Extent map** (`F_LOG2PHYS_EXT`, metadata only) of the installed `packed_experts/layer_NN.bin`: 423–863 extents per 429,916,160 B file, mean extent 0.48–0.97 MiB, **0 of 422–862 extent boundaries physically adjacent**, and **every** production 3,358,720 B read spans 4.30–8.62 extents (max 11). **(2) Serial random `pread`** at production shape — 30 fds, `O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC`, 3,358,720 B at slot-aligned offsets, 12.01 GiB working set, one buffer per read, 300 reads: **mean 2,472 µs, p50 2,443, p10 2,139, p90 2,798 = 1.36 GB/s.** This is bare `pread` with no runtime around it and it matches the in-situ `ce287b6` figure of 2,511–2,592 µs / 1.30–1.34 GB/s, i.e. **the production fetch path achieves 94–96% of what a bare serial read of the same files delivers.** **(3) Queue depth buys nothing:** `dispatch_apply` (the `concurrentPerform` in `executeExpertCachePlan`) at k=2/3/8 gives aggregate 1.55 / 1.43 / 1.52 GB/s against serial 1.36 — flat, so the ~2.6-way fan-out is not leaving parallelism on the table. **(4) Content compressibility is the confound.** Fresh 6 GiB file on the same volume, same probe code, same 18.0 extents/read: **all-zero fill 1,426 µs = 2.36 GB/s; incompressible xorshift fill 4,390 µs = 0.77 GB/s.** Same size, same fragmentation, 3.1× apart. The recorded 2026-08-10 "2.7–3.2 GB/s SSD roof" reproduces only on the zero fill, so that probe's "6 GiB non-sparse file" was near-certainly zero-filled and its number is a storage-stack artifact (zeros never reach NAND at full cost), **not a roof any model byte can reach** — INT4 weights are incompressible, per IO-07 (LZ4 saved 0.06%). Inferred, not directly confirmed: the original probe's fill was not recorded. **(5) The real ceiling for these files:** sequential in file order over 14 layer files (5.61 GiB) = **1.71 GB/s** (1,969 µs/block); random at 1×/2×/4× slot size = 1.39 / 1.58 / 1.63 GB/s. So perfect locality is worth ~1.26× over the random pattern production actually issues, and coalescing is already near its asymptote at 2 slots. **(6) Fragmentation is real but second-order, and preallocation would now backfire:** across the 30 layer files, 2.3× more extents/read (3.67 → 8.62) costs only +11% latency (layers 0–10 mean 2,122 µs vs. layers 23–29 mean 2,352 µs); and a file written *today* on this 92%-full volume lands at 18 extents/read with 0.19 MiB extents, i.e. **worse than the installed files' 4–8**, so CACHE-09 (APFS extent preallocation) would degrade this artifact rather than improve it. **Consequences:** the "largest known quality-free win" in `CLAUDE.md` is withdrawn — `io` has ~4–6% of headroom against its own access pattern, not 2.2×; the only remaining lever on `io` is fewer bytes. And the 16 GB M1 Air's implied **2.04 GB/s exceeds both 1.39 GB/s (random) and 1.71 GB/s (sequential)**, so on an equal SSD it cannot source all expert bytes from storage and ≥32% must come from the page cache — which restores, with corrected demand arithmetic, the conclusion the 2026-08-10 retraction withdrew. Caveats: probes ran with an idle GPU and no concurrent model process, so they bound the fetch path rather than reproduce its environment; the 16 GB host's SSD roof is still assumed equal, not measured; (4) and (6) are two-point comparisons. Not a `real-generation-v1` run — tok/s `n/a`, not comparable to the decode rows. Supersedes the roof figure in the 2026-08-10 `417f389` probe row above. |

Every figure below is preceded by a **12.01 GiB flush read (8× the ~1.44 GB page cache)**; `vm_stat` file-backed pages checked after flush. **(1) Fragmentation does correlate, within one family of files.** Sequential pass1 across 8 installed layer files spanning 3.67–8.62 extents/read: **1.78 / 1.77 / 1.72 / 1.65 / 1.62 / 1.58 / 1.58 / 1.54 GB/s**, near-monotonic — 2.35× more extents costs **−13.5%**, independently replicating the ~11% slope the random-read fit gave by a different method. **(2) But extent count does not survive a cross-file comparison, and neither does any other locality metric.** `model_weights.bin` (7.84 extents/read) vs `layer_25.bin` (7.82) at equal 400 MiB length, flushed, both orderings: **1.85 vs 1.58 GB/s mean, +17%** at statistically identical fragmentation. Read offset ruled out (layer_25 @0 1.48 vs @200M 1.47; layer_09 @0 1.65 vs @200M 1.67). `physorder.c` shows the *fast* file has the *worst* physical ordering — `model_weights.bin` 67.4% forward jumps, mean |jump| 39.6 GiB; `layer_25.bin` 85.9% forward, mean |jump| 1.1 GiB, spread 110× vs 178×.
